messages.subject: Comparing model fit via anova
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to decide whether a theoretically derived (i.e. confirmatory) IRT model fits the data better than some general (i.e. exploratory) IRT model. Specifically, I have 14 binary indicators of outgroup-stereotyping. Our theory suggests that we should have a confirmatory model in which the first seven items load onto the first factor only, and items 8-14 load onto the second factor only, while latent traits should be correlated. Can I simply compare the BIC or similar criteria of this constrained model to an overall one-dimensional exploratory model? I am skeptical because differences in the BIC are HUGE (86311.38 for the confirmatory model as supposed to 201857.93 for the exploratory model).

Many thanks, 

Tobi

On Tue, Jan 20, 2015 at 5:59 PM, Tobias Konitzer <tobias....@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi,

I am trying to decide whether a theoretically derived (i.e. confirmatory) IRT model fits the data better than some general (i.e. exploratory) IRT model. Specifically, I have 14 binary indicators of outgroup-stereotyping. Our theory suggests that we should have a confirmatory model in which the first seven items load onto the first factor only, and items 8-14 load onto the second factor only, while latent traits should be correlated. Can I simply compare the BIC or similar criteria of this constrained model to an overall one-dimensional exploratory model? I am skeptical because differences in the BIC are HUGE (86311.38 for the confirmatory model as supposed to 201857.93 for the exploratory model).

I would be suspicious too, that's a very large difference indeed. Try rotating your exploratory model and inspecting the loading patterns to see how well it does. Also, you could compare how M2() stats look, or how item fit statistics behave with itemfit() to come to similar conclusions. I'm not sure why your exploratory model is so high, I wouldn't expect such a difference in log-likelihoods (it should have a much lower log-likelihood than the confirmatory model; that is, if they have the same number of factors). Cheers.

Phil
 

Many thanks, 

Tobi
